name: LinkedIn Profile Analysis
description: Signals extracted from LinkedIn profiles to evidence DevOps skills. LinkedIn provides professional context, endorsements, and career trajectory data.

sections.notes: Self-described; provides intent and self-assessment context.

sections.description: Work experience entries with job titles, companies, and descriptions.
sections.notes: Similar to CV work experience but often more concise. Look for DevOps-related job titles and descriptions.
quality_indicators: DevOps-related job titles (DevOps Engineer, SRE, Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer)
Company size and industry (enterprise vs startup)

sections.description: Skills listed with endorsement counts from connections.
sections.notes: Endorsements have very low evidential value â€” they can be exchanged socially. However, the skill list provides self-reported skill claims.
Same as CV certifications â€” theoretical knowledge indicator, not practical proof.

sections.description: Projects section with descriptions and links.
sections.notes: Provides additional project context. Links to GitHub or live demos increase strength.

sections.description: Written recommendations from colleagues or managers.
sections.notes: Third-party validation of skills, but often generic. Look for specific technical skill mentions.

sections.description: Technical posts and articles published on LinkedIn.
sections.notes: Indicates thought leadership and depth of knowledge in specific areas.

signal_mapping.description: How LinkedIn mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: Job experience explicitly describing building CI/CD pipelines
Job experience mentioning AWS/Azure/GCP infrastructure management
Detailed project description outlining Terraform infrastructure as code

important_notes: ALL extracted signals MUST be mapped to COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id})
LinkedIn data supplements but should not override GitHub or assessment evidence
Endorsements have near-zero evidential value on their own
Job titles can be inflated â€” cross-reference with actual responsibilities described
Career trajectory (progression from junior to mid to senior roles) provides context
Look for technical content creation (posts, articles) as evidence of deep understanding
